summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath following a recent dialysis session where 5 liters of fluid were removed. He developed worsening pulmonary edema and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, likely triggered by fluid overload. Chest pain persisted but was determined to be musculoskeletal, consistent with costochondritis, rather than acute cardiac injury, as troponin levels were stable and no coronary artery disease was previously found. He underwent hemodialysis, which improved his volume status and respiratory symptoms. His diltiazem was temporarily adjusted to control heart rate, then returned to extended-release dosing. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, adhere to fluid restrictions, monitor weight, and take prescribed medications including acetaminophen for chest pain.
